paper.title_en: Exploring charmonia \(\eta_{c}(6S,7S)\) in the \(\Lambda_{c}^{+}\overline{\Lambda}\,_{c}^{-}\) invariant mass spectrum of \(B^{0}\rightarrow K_{S}^{0}\Lambda_{c}^{+}\overline{\Lambda}\,{}_{c}^{-}\)
paper.abstract_en: We analyze the \(B^{0}\rightarrow K_{S}^{0}\Lambda_{c}^{+}\overline{\Lambda}\,_{c}^{-}\) decay recently observed by the LHCb Collaboration. The \(\Lambda_{c}^{+}\overline{\Lambda}\,_{c}^{-}\) invariant-mass spectrum exhibits an accumulation near 4.63 GeV, which we investigate together with the accompanying \(\Lambda_{c}^{+}K_{S}^{0}\) spectrum constrained by the known \(\Xi_{c}(2923)\) and \(\Xi_{c}(2939)\) states. Our amplitude model includes a nonresonant term, the two established \(\Xi_{c}\) contributions, and high-lying charmonium states in the \(\Lambda_{c}^{+}\overline{\Lambda}\,_{c}^{-}\) channel. Guided by screened Godfrey-Isgur and quark-pair-creation calculations, we test the 4.63 GeV enhancement with a fixed \(\eta_{c}(6S)\) amplitude at \((M_{1},\Gamma_{1}) = (4629.00,24.20)\,\,\text{MeV}\), which improves the description of the 4.63 GeV region, and examine a fixed \(\eta_{c}(7S)\) contribution at \((M_{2},\Gamma_{2}) = (4718.84,22.84)\,\,\text{MeV}\), which improves the higher-mass region of the spectrum. We also evaluate the \(\eta_{c}(nS)\rightarrow\Lambda_{c}^{+}\overline{\Lambda}\,_{c}^{-}\) baryonic decays via a hadron-loop mechanism and estimate the \(B^{0}\rightarrow K_{S}^{0}\eta_{c}(nS)\) production in naive factorization. Within the narrow width approximation, the fit yields a \(\mathcal{B}(B^{0}\rightarrow K_{S}^{0}\eta_{c}(6S)) \times \mathcal{B}(\eta_{c}(6S)\rightarrow\Lambda_{c}^{+}\overline{\Lambda}\,_{c}^{-})\) of about \(6.2 \times 10^{- 6}\), while the factorization and hadron-loop calculations give rates roughly one to three orders of magnitude lower than the above fitted ratio. These results highlight the need for more precise data and a full amplitude analysis to determine the line shapes and clarify the nature of the higher-mass contribution.
